title: Swap the hotend on a Bambu Lab A1 mini 3D printer: buckle open, old hotend to its holder, new one seated, locked
instruction: Change the 3D printer's hotend: open the buckle, take the old hotend out and stand it in the empty slot of the holder, then push the new hotend up into the toolhead until it seats and lock the buckle.
context: Low-cost robot arms are built from printed parts: the SO-ARM100 printing guide (LeRobot) lists Bambu Lab A/P/X-series printers, and XLeRobot's parts were printed on a Bambu Lab A1. The printers that make those parts need hotend swaps to clear clogs, replace worn or damaged nozzles or change size (0.2 mm for fine detail, 0.4 mm standard, hardened steel for abrasive filament), done by lab and makerspace staff and print-farm technicians. Bambu's procedure for the A1 series (wiki: Hotend Replacement for A1 Series; the A1 mini takes the same hotend): with the printer off and cool, the filament cut and the front cover and silicone sock off, push the nozzle buckle to unlock it and swing it open, hold the heatsink and pull the hotend out, put the new one in until it sits flush (a magnet aligns it) and close the buckle; if the buckle will not lock, the hotend is not seated. The hard part: seating a small part overhead, half hidden under the toolhead, between unlocking and locking.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left); heights above the table. Bambu Lab A1 mini 3D printer, powered off and cold, front toward the robot; a loose 5.5 kg block model: base 28 x 24 x 7 cm (x 27.5 to 55.5, y -12 to 12) with an 18 x 18 cm bed (top 7.6 cm up); Z column 6 x 5 x 31 cm at the right rear (x 46.5 to 52.5, y -17 to -12); X arm 3 x 25 x 3 cm behind the toolhead, 25 to 28 cm up. Toolhead (front cover and silicone sock off, filament cut): 3.5 x 5.4 x 7.5 cm, x 36.5 to 40, y -2.7 to 2.7, underside 20 cm up; in it a 1.5 x 2.1 cm hotend pocket 1.2 cm deep at x 37.5, y 0, with a 1.4 cm wide, 1.1 cm high window in its front wall, and a sprung catch in its back wall that presses the hotend forward with about 0.4 N (for the A1's magnet). Buckle: a 2.8 cm metal bar on a vertical hinge at x 36.3, y -1.2 (the window's right), 20.2 to 20.5 cm up, with a 1.2 x 1 x 0.7 cm tab at its left end; closed it lies along the window under the hotend's lug; its left end swings out to the front, up to 90 degrees. Two Bambu Hotend - A1 Series hotends, each simplified to a 1.2 x 1.8 x 4.6 cm heatsink with a 0.7 x 1 x 0.4 cm lug on its front just below the top and a 0.7 cm nozzle, 6 cm overall, 22 g: the old one (0.4 mm, dark band) seated in the pocket; the new one (0.2 mm, green tag) standing nozzle-down in the holder's right slot. Holder: printed PLA, 200 g, loose: a 4 x 16 x 8 cm block (x 23 to 27, y -5 to 11) with two 1.1 x 1.8 x 2 cm bosses on top (tops 10 cm up), each with a 0.9 cm square hole: the right slot at y -3.5 (new hotend), the left one at y 9.5 (empty). Real trial: place the A1 mini so the installed hotend's axis is at x 37.5, y 0, with the toolhead's underside 20 cm up (set Z before powering off); stand the holder in front of the printer (against its front edge if the real base reaches past x 27), slots at y -3.5 and 9.5.
scoring: Score = 0.2 x old out + 0.4 x new seated + 0.3 x locked + 0.1 x finished; 0 if the new hotend is dropped. Old out: the old hotend stands in a holder slot (either; only the left one is free at the start; axis within 0.3 cm of the slot's, heatsink on the boss within 0.3 cm, within 8 degrees of upright) and was not dropped on the way. Dropped: a hotend falls 2 cm within 0.5 s with no finger pad within 1.5 cm of its heatsink while not in the pocket or a slot, or its nozzle tip reaches the bed or the table. New seated: the new hotend's top within 0.15 cm of the pocket's top, its axis within 0.25 cm of the seat and within 4 degrees of vertical. Locked: the buckle within 3 degrees of its closed stop while the new hotend is seated (closed, its bar lies 0.15 cm under a seated hotend's lug). The catch holds a hotend only once it is pushed fully home: one let go short of its seat slides out and falls. Finished: seated and locked, no finger pad within 1 cm of the new hotend's heatsink or the buckle's tab, and the new hotend still (under 0.15 cm of motion) for 20 steps (1 s); the run is a success, and ends, once that has held 1 s with the old hotend in a slot. Real trial, from photos and the video: old out = standing upright in either holder slot (end photo); locked = the buckle closed and latched in the end photo; finished = no part of either gripper touches the new hotend or the buckle in the last 1 s (video); seated = after the end photo, a strip of printer paper (about 0.1 mm) does not slide between the heatsink and the heating assembly, and the buckle locks over it (Bambu: it will not lock over an unseated hotend; if the robot left it open, the scorer closes it by hand without touching the hotend, which does not earn 'locked'); dropped = the new hotend falls or is set down on the bed, the table or the floor.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Put the old hotend back in the pocket and close and lock the buckle, stand the new hotend in the holder's right slot, and put the printer and the holder back on their tape marks. Real trials: the printer stays off and cool (below 50 C) with the front cover and silicone sock off and the filament cut; powered off, its toolhead slides along the X arm, so slide it back to its tape mark (hotend axis at y 0) before each trial; the two hotends may swap roles between trials.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The printer is a loose 5.5 kg block model with its toolhead fixed to it (the real carriage slides along X). The hotend is simplified: 6 cm long (real 4.73 cm), 1.2 x 1.8 cm heatsink, 22 g (est.). The A1's magnet, which pulls the hotend back flush against the heater, is a 1.2 cm deep pocket with a sprung catch (about 0.4 N) holding it by friction; the buckle is a hinged bar closing 0.15 cm under the hotend's lug. Not simulated: the buckle's push to unlock and its right-side lock.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2,400 steps; right gripper went to the toolhead's front, left arm reached over the printer, buckle never opened); demo: 1.0 (868 steps; scripted, both arms)
